arxiv-2012-11075.title: Well-balanced lattice Boltzmann equation for two-phase flows
arxiv-2012-11075.creator: Zhaoli Guo
arxiv-2012-11075.description: Abstract The standard lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE) method usually fails to capture the physical equilibrium state of a two-phase fluid system, i.e., zero velocity and constant chemical potential. Consequently, spurious velocities and inconsistent thermodynamic density properties are frequently encountered in LBE simulations.

arxiv-2102-05766.title: Fused Acoustic and Text Encoding for Multimodal Bilingual Pretraining and Speech Translation
arxiv-2102-05766.creator: Renjie Zheng, Junkun Chen, Mingbo Ma, Liang Huang
arxiv-2102-05766.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Renjie Zheng, Junkun Chen, Mingbo Ma, Liang Huang. Recently, representation learning for text and speech has successfully improved many language related tasks. However, all existing methods suffer from two limitations: (a) they only learn from one input modality, while a unified representation for both speech and text is needed by tasks such as end-to-end speech translation, and as a result, (b) they can not exploit various large-scale text and speech data and their performance is limited by the scarcity of parallel speech translation data.

arxiv-2407-16577.title: Non-local Nucleon Matrix Elements in the Rest Frame
arxiv-2407-16577.creator: Joe Karpie, Christopher Monahan, Anatoly Radyushkin
arxiv-2407-16577.description: Abstract Extracting parton structure from lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculations requires studying the coordinate scale z 3 z_{3} dependence of the matrix elements of bilocal operators. The most significant contribution comes from the z 3 z_{3} dependence induced by ultraviolet (UV) renormalization of the Wilson line.

arxiv-2507-04382.title: The Hybrid Elevated Radio Observatory for Neutrinos (HERON) Project
arxiv-2507-04382.creator: Andrew Zeolla
arxiv-2507-04382.description: Abstract Measuring ultra-high energy neutrinos, with energies above 10 16 10^{16} eV, is the next frontier of the emerging multi-messenger era. Their detection requires building a large-scale detector with 10 times the instantaneous sensitivity of current instruments, sub-degree angular resolution, and wide daily field of view.

arxiv-2509-16866.title: seqBench : A Tunable Benchmark to Quantify Sequential Reasoning Limits of LLMs
arxiv-2509-16866.creator: M.R. Ramezanali, M. Vazifeh, P. Santi

pmc-11235026.title: Cardiovascular health: an important component of cancer survivorship
pmc-11235026.creator: Siobhan Cleary, Stuart D Rosen, Duncan C Gilbert, Ruth E Langley
pmc-11235026.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Advances in the detection and treatment of cancer have translated into improved cancer survival rates and a growing population of cancer survivors. These include those living with cancer and individuals free of the disease following treatment. Epidemiological studies demonstrate that cancer survivors are at an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), with cardiovascular (CV) mortality overtaking cancer mortality in some tumour types.

pmc-11354778.title: Wilson’s Disease—Crossroads of Genetics, Inflammation and Immunity/Autoimmunity: Clinical and Molecular Issues
pmc-11354778.creator: Grażyna Gromadzka, Julia Czerwińska, Elżbieta Krzemińska, Adam Przybyłkowski, Tomasz Litwin
pmc-11354778.description: Wilson’s disease (WD) is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder of copper metabolism caused by pathogenic mutations in the ATP7B gene. Cellular copper overload is associated with impaired iron metabolism. Oxidative stress, cuproptosis, and ferroptosis are involved in cell death in WD. The clinical picture of WD is variable. Hepatic/neuropsychiatric/other symptoms may manifest in childhood/adulthood and even old age.

pmc-11391760.title: Curriculum, competency development, and assessment methods of MSc and PhD pharmacy programs: a scoping review
pmc-11391760.creator: Dana ElKhalifa, Ola Hussein, Abeer Hamid, Nour Al-Ziftawi, Israa Al-Hashimi, Mohamed Izham Mohamed Ibrahim
pmc-11391760.description: Background/objectivesWe aim to systematically review and evaluate the current landscape of postgraduate pharmacy education to a) identify current evidence, best practices, challenges, recommendations, and solutions; and b) develop a framework to optimize postgraduate pharmacy programs.MethodsA scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

pmc-11521831.title: Were there any missing mediators between visual impairment and anxiety symptoms? Results from Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey
pmc-11521831.creator: Wen Yao, Yuan Cao, Yuan Tian, Yuanyuan Liu, Xin Hua, Fang Chen
pmc-11521831.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionVisual impairment, encompassing low visual acuity and visual field loss, significantly impacts the older adult population worldwide, leading to increased disability and mortality risks. Recent studies suggest a strong association between visual impairment and anxiety, particularly among older adults.

pmc-11634739.title: Stiffening symphony of aging: Biophysical changes in senescent osteocytes
pmc-11634739.creator: Maryam Tilton, Megan Weivoda, Maria Astudillo Potes, Anne Gingery, Alan Y. Liu, Tamara Tchkonia, Lichun Lu, James L. Kirkland
pmc-11634739.description: Senescent osteocytes are key contributors to age‐related bone loss and fragility; however, the impact of mechanobiological changes in these cells remains poorly understood. This study provides a novel analysis of these changes in primary osteocytes following irradiation‐induced senescence. By integrating subcellular mechanical measurements with gene expression analyses, we identified significant, time‐dependent alterations in the mechanical properties of senescent bone cells.

pmc-11677402.title: Microbiological Aspects and Enzymatic Characterization of Curvularia kusanoi L7: Ascomycete with Great Biomass Degradation Potentialities
pmc-11677402.creator: Maryen Alberto Vazquez, Luis Rodrigo Saa, Elaine Valiño, Livio Torta, Vito Armando Laudicina, Fabio Squina
pmc-11677402.description: The complex structure of the plant cell wall makes it difficult to use the biomass produced by biosynthesis. For this reason, the search for new strains of microorganisms capable of efficiently degrading fiber is a topic of interest. For these reasons, the present study aimed to evaluate both the microbiological and enzymatic characteristics of the fungus Curvularia kusanoi L7strain.

pmc-12464050.title: Editorial: Management of spine pathologies in geriatric patients
pmc-12464050.creator: Ismail Zaed, Gabriele Capo, Aria Nouri, Luca Ricciardi
pmc-12464050.description: iagnosis and anesthesia to intervention, complication surveillance, and rehabilitation—to help clinicians individualize decisions for geriatric patients with spine disease. The eight contributions collected here move the field forward in four overarching ways: (1) sharpening risk prediction, (2) elevating peri-procedural safety, and (3) testing realistic rehabilitative and non-pharmacologic strategies, while also spotlighting emerging (4) diagnostic tools.

pmc-12951963.title: Transposable elements contribute to the evolution of host shift–related genes in cactophilic Drosophila species
pmc-12951963.creator: Daniel Siqueira de Oliveira, Anaïs Larue, William Vilas Boas Nunes, Francois Sabot, Alejandra Bodelón, María Pilar García Guerreiro, Cristina Vieira, Claudia Marcia Aparecida Carareto
pmc-12951963.description: Host shifts in insects are considered a key process with the potential to contribute to reproductive isolation and speciation. Both genomic and transcriptomic variation are attributed to such a process, in which gene families with functions associated with host localization, acceptance, and usage are proposed to evolve.

pmc-13087760.title: Protocol to predict gene expression from transcriptomic data using PREDICT
pmc-13087760.creator: Ming-Ren Yen, Kai-Cheng Pan, Ming-Jung Liu, Chia-Yi Cheng, Ting-Ying Wu
pmc-13087760.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryLinking DNA sequence variation to context-specific transcriptional programs is a critical challenge in regulatory genomics, especially for non-model organisms. Here, we present PREDICT, a modular Python package for discovering cis-regulatory elements and transcription factor binding motifs. We describe steps to identify enriched k-mers from differentially expressed genes, map them to known motifs, quantify their impact on gene expression, and visualize motif co-occurrences.

pmc-13129103.title: Embryonic zeolite-mediated suture synthesis of thin and scalable zeolite membranes for tailored gas separation
pmc-13129103.creator: Lekai You, Yang Jin, Zerui Zhu, Xingyu Peng, Yuanxing Fan, Freek Kapteijn, Xuerui Wang, Xuehong Gu
pmc-13129103.description: Zeolite membranes exhibit considerable potential for gas separation; however, two critical challenges (low permeation flux and scaling-up fabrication) continue to hinder their practical implementation. Here, we propose an embryonic zeolite-mediated suture (EZMS) strategy to synthesize large-area zeolite membranes with stable gas separation performance.

pmc-13236890.title: Human iPSC-derived motor neurons as a platform for elucidating TDP-43-related amyotrophic lateral sclerosis pathogenesis: a mini review
pmc-13236890.creator: Satoshi Yokoi, Yohei Iguchi, Masahisa Katsuno
pmc-13236890.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a major pathogenic RNA-binding protein associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Heterozygous mutations in TDP-43 cause familial ALS, known as ALS10. TDP-43 is predominantly localized in the nucleus under physiological conditions. Not only ALS patients with TARDBP mutations but also the majority of sporadic ALS patients exhibit TDP-43 pathology, which is defined by nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic aggregation.

pmc-13674166.title: Identifying a Cardio‐Hepatic Phenotype by Integrating the Albumin‐Bilirubin Score Into Risk Assessment in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
pmc-13674166.creator: Hacer Ceren Tokgoz, Barkin Kultursay, Seda Tanyeri, Dicle Sırma, Cagdas Bulus, Tezel Kovanci, Mustafa Kara, Seyma Zeynep Atici, Seyma Nur Cicek, Caglar Emre Cagliyan, Azmican Kaya, Faruk Akalin, Dogan Sen, Leyla Aliyeva, Nihal Ozdemir, Cihangir Kaymaz
pmc-13674166.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Risk stratification is essential in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet the prognostic utility of the albumin‐bilirubin (ALBI) score as a marker of hepatic dysfunction remains underexplored. In this single‐center study, we evaluated the clinical, neurohumoral, echocardiographic and hemodynamic correlates and prognostic value of the ALBI score, and to assess whether this score offers an incremental benefit over the Registry to EValuate Early And Long‐term pulmonary arterial hypertension disease management (REVEAL) 2.0 risk score in patients with PAH.

pmc-13685135.title: Acceptability of Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) in neonatal transport: a qualitative study on mothers’ and healthcare professionals’ perspectives on KMC transport in Ghana
pmc-13685135.creator: Emmanuel Okai, Frankie Fair, Hilda Danquah Konadu, Prince Arkoh, Evans Ntim, Eugene K M Darteh, Hora Soltani
pmc-13685135.description: BackgroundIn limited-resource settings, the lack of ambulances and transport incubators increases the risk of adverse outcomes in transported preterm and low-birth-weight neonates. The Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) position during transport using available transport modes may be a cost-effective alternative. Mothers’ and healthcare professionals’ perspectives on the intervention are key to its successful implementation.

pmc-13686567.title: Assessing the reproducibility of a bioimage analysis workflow characterising tissue flow in Drosophila
pmc-13686567.creator: Mélodie Ambroset, Cesar Augusto Valades‐Cruz, Libert Brice Tonfack, Rocco D'Antuono, Caterina Fuster‐Barceló
pmc-13686567.description: Reproducibility challenges in bioimage analysis are common. The proliferation of tools and workflows creates a complex ecosystem that is difficult to reproduce without deliberate, explicit reporting and support.We assess the reproducibility of Gehrels et al.(2023) as a representative bioimage analysis workflow.
